sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā sītā raudrasya rakṣasaḥ ārtā dīnasvarā dīnaṃ pratyuvāca śanair vacaḥ
english: Having heard the words of that fierce rākṣasa, Sītā, afflicted and with a pitiful voice, softly spoke words of distress in reply.

sanskrit: duḥkhārtā rudatī sītā vepamānā tapasvinī cintayantī varārohā patim eva pativratā
english: Sītā, tormented by grief, weeping, trembling, that afflicted woman of noble bearing — devoted wife that she was — thought only of her husband.

sanskrit: tṛṇam antarataḥ kṛtvā pratyuvāca śucismitā nivartaya mano mattaḥ svajane kriyatāṃ manaḥ
english: Placing a blade of grass between herself and him, she of pure smile replied: "Turn your mind away from me; fix your mind instead upon your own people."

sanskrit: na māṃ prārthayituṃ yuktas tvaṃ siddhim iva pāpakṛt akāryaṃ na mayā kāryam ekapatnyā vigarhitam kulaṃ saṃprāptayā puṇyaṃ kule mahati jātayā
english: "You are no more fit to desire me than a sinner is fit to attain liberation. I shall not do what must not be done — I am a woman of one husband; having reached a censurable family, born myself in a great and virtuous lineage."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu vaidehī rāvaṇaṃ taṃ yaśasvinī rākṣasaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā bhūyo vacanam abravīt
english: Having spoken thus, Vaidehī — that illustrious woman — turned her back on that rākṣasa Rāvaṇa and spoke again.

sanskrit: nāham aupayikī bhāryā parabhāryā satī tava sādhu dharmam avekṣasva sādhu sādhuvrataṃ cara
english: "I am another man's wife — I am not a fitting wife for you. Look to righteousness properly; observe the vow of the virtuous properly."

sanskrit: yathā tava tathānyeṣāṃ rakṣyā dārā niśācara ātmānam upamāṃ kṛtvā sveṣu dāreṣu ramyatām
english: "Just as your own wives are to be protected, so too are the wives of others, O night-wanderer. Taking yourself as the measure, find delight with your own wives."

sanskrit: atuṣṭaṃ sveṣu dāreṣu capalaṃ calitendriyam nayanti nikṛtiprajñāṃ paradārāḥ parābhavam
english: "The wives of other men bring ruin to one who is unsatisfied with his own wives, who is fickle with unsteady senses, whose understanding is base."

sanskrit: iha santo na vā santi sato vā nānuvartase vaco mithyā praṇītātmā pathyam uktaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ
english: "Either there are no virtuous men here, or you do not heed the virtuous — your soul is led astray, and you do not follow what the wise have declared to be salutary."

sanskrit: akṛtātmānam āsādya rājānam anaye ratam samṛddhāni vinaśyanti rāṣṭrāṇi nagarāṇi ca
english: "Prosperous kingdoms and cities perish when they obtain a king who has not mastered himself and who delights in unrighteousness."

sanskrit: tatheyaṃ tvāṃ samāsādya laṅkā ratnaugha saṃkulā aparādhāt tavaikasya nacirād vinaśiṣyati
english: "So too will this Laṅkā, filled with multitudes of jewels, soon perish because of your single transgression."

sanskrit: svakṛtair hanyamānasya rāvaṇādīrghadarśinaḥ abhinandanti bhūtāni vināśe pāpakarmaṇaḥ
english: "When one of evil deeds is being slain by the fruits of his own actions, O Rāvaṇa of short sight, all creatures rejoice at his destruction."

sanskrit: evaṃ tvāṃ pāpakarmāṇaṃ vakṣyanti nikṛtā janāḥ diṣṭyaitad vyasanaṃ prāpto raudra ity eva harṣitāḥ
english: "Thus will wronged people speak of you, the evil-doer, rejoicing: 'By fate this calamity has come upon the fierce one.'"

sanskrit: śakyā lobhayituṃ nāham aiśvaryeṇa dhanena vā ananyā rāghaveṇāhaṃ bhāskareṇa prabhā yathā
english: "I cannot be tempted by sovereignty or wealth. I am inseparable from Rāghava, as radiance is inseparable from the sun."

sanskrit: upadhāya bhujaṃ tasya lokanāthasya satkṛtam kathaṃ nāmopadhāsyāmi bhujam anyasya kasya cit
english: "Having rested my head upon the honored arm of that lord of the world, how could I ever rest it upon the arm of any other?"

sanskrit: aham aupayikī bhāryā tasyaiva vasudhāpateḥ vratasnātasya viprasya vidyeva viditātmanaḥ
english: "I am the fitting wife of that lord of the earth alone — as sacred learning belongs to a brahmin who has bathed at the completion of his vow and who has known the Self."

sanskrit: sādhu rāvaṇa rāmeṇa māṃ samānaya duḥkhitām vane vāśitayā sārdhaṃ kareṇveva gajādhipam
english: "Do right, Rāvaṇa: restore me, afflicted as I am, to Rāma, as the lord of elephants returns to his she-elephant calling in the forest."

sanskrit: mitram aupayikaṃ kartuṃ rāmaḥ sthānaṃ parīpsatā vadhaṃ cānicchatā ghoraṃ tvayāsau puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: "That bull among men, Rāma, is one whose friendship is well worth seeking by you who desire your position to endure and who would avoid a terrible death."

sanskrit: varjayed vajram utsṛṣṭaṃ varjayed antakaś ciram tvadvidhaṃ na tu saṃkruddho lokanāthaḥ sa rāghavaḥ
english: "One might escape the thunderbolt once hurled; one might long escape Death itself — but that Rāghava, lord of the world, when enraged, one of your kind could not escape."

sanskrit: rāmasya dhanuṣaḥ śabdaṃ śroṣyasi tvaṃ mahāsvanam śatakratuvisṛṣṭasya nirghoṣam aśaner iva
english: "You will hear the great roar of Rāma's bow — like the crash of a thunderbolt released by Indra of a hundred sacrifices."

sanskrit: iha śīghraṃ suparvāṇo jvalitāsyā ivoragāḥ iṣavo nipatiṣyanti rāmalakṣmaṇalakṣaṇāḥ
english: "Here, soon, arrows bearing the mark of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa — well-jointed, with blazing heads like serpents — will rain down."

sanskrit: rakṣāṃsi parinighnantaḥ puryām asyāṃ samantataḥ asaṃpātaṃ kariṣyanti patantaḥ kaṅkavāsasaḥ
english: "Those arrows, feathered with vulture-plumes, falling everywhere in this city and slaying rākṣasas on all sides, will leave no room for flight."

sanskrit: rākṣasendramahāsarpān sa rāmagaruḍo mahān uddhariṣyati vegena vainateya ivoragān
english: "That great Garuḍa Rāma will swiftly pluck up the great serpents that are the lords of the rākṣasas, as Vainateya plucks up serpents."

sanskrit: apaneṣyati māṃ bhartā tvattaḥ śīghram ariṃdamaḥ asurebhyaḥ śriyaṃ dīptāṃ viṣṇus tribhir iva kramaiḥ
english: "My husband, the subduer of foes, will swiftly recover me from you, as Viṣṇu recovered the blazing royal splendor from the asuras with his three strides."

sanskrit: janasthāne hatasthāne nihate rakṣasāṃ bale aśaktena tvayā rakṣaḥ kṛtam etad asādhu vai
english: "In Janasthāna, that destroyed place, when the host of rākṣasas was slain, this evil deed was done by you who were powerless to face them directly."

sanskrit: āśramaṃ tu tayoḥ śūnyaṃ praviśya narasiṃhayoḥ gocaraṃ gatayor bhrātror apanītā tvayādhama
english: "Entering the empty hermitage of those two lion-men while the two brothers had gone to their hunting grounds — thus were you able to carry me off, O vile one."

sanskrit: na hi gandham upāghrāya rāmalakṣmaṇayos tvayā śakyaṃ saṃdarśane sthātuṃ śunā śārdūlayor iva
english: "You could no more stand in the presence of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa — having merely caught their scent — than a dog could stand before two tigers."

sanskrit: tasya te vigrahe tābhyāṃ yugagrahaṇam asthiram vṛtrasyevendrabāhubhyāṃ bāhor ekasya nigrahaḥ
english: "In battle against those two, your wrestling hold would be as unstable as the seizure of Indra's arms by Vṛtra — only to be overcome by a single arm."

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ tava sa nātho me rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha toyam alpam ivādityaḥ prāṇān ādāsyate śaraiḥ
english: "That lord of mine, Rāma, together with Saumitrī, will swiftly take your life with his arrows, as the sun dries up a small pool of water."

sanskrit: giriṃ kuberasya gato 'tha vālayaṃ sabhāṃ gato vā varuṇasya rājñaḥ asaṃśayaṃ dāśarather na mokṣyase mahādrumaḥ kālahato 'śaner iva
english: "Whether you go to Kubera's mountain or to Vālin's realm, or enter the court of King Varuṇa — you will assuredly not escape from the son of Daśaratha, as a great tree struck down by time does not escape the thunderbolt."

sanskrit: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā paruṣaṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ pratyuvāca tataḥ sītāṃ vipriyaṃ priyadarśanām
english: Having heard Sītā's harsh words, the lord of rākṣasas then replied to Sītā — that beautiful-looking woman — with words she would not wish to hear.

sanskrit: yathā yathā sāntvayitā vaśyaḥ strīṇāṃ tathā tathā yathā yathā priyaṃ vaktā paribhūtas tathā tathā
english: "The more a man is gentle and yielding to women, the more he is dominated; the more he speaks what is pleasing, the more he is treated with contempt."

sanskrit: saṃniyacchati me krodhaṃ tvayi kāmaḥ samutthitaḥ dravato mārgam āsādya hayān iva susārathiḥ
english: "The desire that has arisen for you restrains my anger, as a skilled charioteer controls galloping horses on the road."

sanskrit: vāmaḥ kāmo manuṣyāṇāṃ yasmin kila nibadhyate jane tasmiṃs tv anukrośaḥ snehaś ca kila jāyate
english: "Love is perverse among humans — it is said that toward the very person in whom one is bound by passion, compassion and affection arise."

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇān na tāṃ ghatayāmi varānane vadhārhām avamānārhāṃ mithyāpravrajite ratām
english: "For this reason I do not destroy you, O beautiful-faced one — though you deserve death and disgrace, you who delight in a false renunciation."

sanskrit: paruṣāṇi hi vākyāni yāni yāni bravīṣi mām teṣu teṣu vadho yuktas tava maithili dāruṇaḥ
english: "For each and every harsh word you speak to me, a terrible death would befit you, O Maithilī."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu vaidehīṃ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ krodhasaṃrambhasaṃyuktaḥ sītām uttaram abravīt
english: Having spoken thus to Vaidehī, Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, filled with the fury of anger, spoke further to Sītā.

sanskrit: dvau māsau rakṣitavyau me yo 'vadhis te mayā kṛtaḥ tataḥ śayanam āroha mama tvaṃ varavarṇini
english: "Two months — the term I have set for you — are to be preserved by me. After that, O woman of splendid complexion, you must ascend my bed."

sanskrit: dvābhyām ūrdhvaṃ tu māsābhyāṃ bhartāraṃ mām anicchatīm mama tvāṃ prātarāśārtham ārabhante mahānase
english: "If, after two months have passed, you still refuse to take me as your husband, my cooks will prepare you as my morning meal."

sanskrit: tāṃ tarjyamānāṃ saṃprekṣya rākṣasendreṇa jānakīm devagandharvakanyās tā viṣedur vipulekṣaṇāḥ
english: Seeing Jānakī being threatened by the lord of rākṣasas, those large-eyed daughters of gods and gandharvas were deeply distressed.

sanskrit: oṣṭhaprakārair aparā netravaktrais tathāparāḥ sītām āśvāsayām āsus tarjitāṃ tena rakṣasā
english: Some comforted Sītā — thus threatened by that rākṣasa — with gestures of their lips, others with expressions of their eyes and faces.

sanskrit: tābhir āśvāsitā sītā rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam uvācātmahitaṃ vākyaṃ vṛttaśauṇḍīryagarvitam
english: Comforted by them, Sītā spoke words beneficial to herself to Rāvaṇa, the lord of rākṣasas, proud of her conduct and virtue.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ na te janaḥ kaś cid asin niḥśreyase sthitaḥ nivārayati yo na tvāṃ karmaṇo 'smād vigarhitāt
english: "Surely there is no one in your company who stands devoted to your highest good — no one who restrains you from this censurable deed."

sanskrit: māṃ hi dharmātmanaḥ patnīṃ śacīm iva śacīpateḥ tvadanyas triṣu lokeṣu prārthayen manasāpi kaḥ
english: "Who other than you in all three worlds would even desire me in his mind — the wife of the righteous-souled one, as Śacī belongs to her lord Indra?"

sanskrit: rākṣasādhama rāmasya bhāryām amitatejasaḥ uktavān asi yat pāpaṃ kva gatas tasya mokṣyase
english: "O vilest of rākṣasas, you have spoken sin against the wife of Rāma of boundless glory — wherever you flee, how will you escape its consequence?"

sanskrit: yathā dṛptaś ca mātaṅgaḥ śaśaś ca sahitau vane tathā dviradavad rāmas tvaṃ nīca śaśavat smṛtaḥ
english: "As a proud elephant and a hare stand together in the forest, so Rāma is to be reckoned as the elephant and you, O lowly one, as the hare."

sanskrit: sa tvam ikṣvākunāthaṃ vai kṣipann iha na lajjase cakṣuṣo viṣayaṃ tasya na tāvad upagacchasi
english: "You who revile the lord of the Ikṣvākus here feel no shame — you have not even come within range of his sight."

sanskrit: ime te nayane krūre virūpe kṛṣṇapiṅgale kṣitau na patite kasmān mām anāryanirīkṣitaḥ
english: "These cruel, ugly, dark-reddish eyes of yours — why have they not fallen to the ground, since with them, unworthy as you are, you have gazed at me?"

sanskrit: tasya dharmātmanaḥ patnīṃ snuṣāṃ daśarathasya ca kathaṃ vyāharato māṃ te na jihvā pāpa śīryate
english: "O sinner, how does your tongue not crumble as you address me — the wife of that righteous-souled one, the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha?"

sanskrit: asaṃdeśāt tu rāmasya tapasaś cānupālanāt na tvāṃ kurmi daśagrīva bhasma bhasmārhatejasā
english: "Only because Rāma has given me no such command, and out of preservation of my austerity, do I not reduce you, O ten-necked one, to ashes with my own blazing power."

sanskrit: nāpahartum ahaṃ śakyā tasya rāmasya dhīmataḥ vidhis tava vadhārthāya vihito nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "I cannot truly be carried off from that wise Rāma. Fate has ordained your destruction — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: śūreṇa dhanadabhrātā balaiḥ samuditena ca apohya rāmaṃ kasmād dhi dāracauryaṃ tvayā kṛtam
english: "You who are the brother of Kubera, endowed with heroism and forces — why did you resort to the theft of a wife by luring Rāma away?"

sanskrit: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ vivṛtya nayane krūre jānakīm anvavaikṣata
english: Having heard Sītā's words, Rāvaṇa, the lord of rākṣasas, widening his cruel eyes, gazed at Jānakī.

sanskrit: nīlajīmūtasaṃkāśo mahābhujaśirodharaḥ siṃhasattvagatiḥ śrīmān dīptajihvogralocanaḥ
english: He was dark as a storm-cloud, with mighty arms and neck, moving with the bearing of a lion, resplendent, with a flaming tongue and fierce eyes.

sanskrit: calāgramakuṭaḥ prāṃśuś citramālyānulepanaḥ raktamālyāmbaradharas taptāṅgadavibhūṣaṇaḥ
english: His towering crown swayed; he was tall, adorned with variegated garlands and unguents, wearing red garlands and garments, and ornamented with blazing armlets.

sanskrit: śroṇīsūtreṇa mahatā mekakena susaṃvṛtaḥ amṛtotpādanaddhena bhujaṃgeneva mandaraḥ
english: He was well girt with a great waist-cord made with the mekaka-jewel, bound with the serpent that had produced the nectar of immortality, like Mount Mandara encircled by a serpent.

sanskrit: taruṇādityavarṇābhyāṃ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ vibhūṣitaḥ raktapallavapuṣpābhyām aśokābhyām ivācalaḥ
english: He was adorned with earrings the color of the newly-risen sun, like a mountain adorned with red-tipped blossoms of the aśoka tree.

sanskrit: avekṣamāṇo vaidehīṃ kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ uvāca rāvaṇaḥ sītāṃ bhujaṃga iva niḥśvasan
english: Gazing at Vaidehī with eyes reddened by anger, Rāvaṇa spoke to Sītā, hissing like a serpent.

sanskrit: anayenābhisaṃpannam arthahīnam anuvrate nāśayāmy aham adya tvāṃ sūryaḥ saṃdhyām ivaujasā
english: "You who are possessed of unrighteousness, bereft of good judgment, following your vow — I shall destroy you this very day, as the sun destroys the twilight with his brilliance."

sanskrit: ity uktvā maithilīṃ rājā rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ saṃdideśa tataḥ sarvā rākṣasīr ghoradarśanāḥ
english: Having spoken thus to Maithilī, King Rāvaṇa — the destroyer of enemies — then commanded all the rākṣasī guards of terrible appearance.

sanskrit: ekākṣīm ekakarṇāṃ ca karṇaprāvaraṇāṃ tathā gokarṇīṃ hastikarṇīṃ ca lambakarṇīm akarṇikām
english: He commanded the one-eyed one, the one-eared one, and the one whose ears served as a cloak; the cow-eared, the elephant-eared, the pendant-eared, and the earless one.

sanskrit: hastipadya śvapadyau ca gopadīṃ pādacūlikām ekākṣīm ekapādīṃ ca pṛthupādīm apādikām
english: He commanded the elephant-footed ones, the dog-footed ones, the cow-footed, and the one with feet small as a talon; the one-eyed one, the one-legged, the broad-footed, and the footless.

sanskrit: atimātraśirogrīvām atimātrakucodarīm atimātrāsyanetrāṃ ca dīrghajihvām ajihvikām anāsikāṃ siṃhamukhīṃ gomukhīṃ sūkarīmukhīm
english: He commanded those with exceedingly large heads and necks, those with exceedingly large breasts and bellies, those with exceedingly large mouths and eyes; the long-tongued, the tongueless, the noseless, those with lion-faces, cow-faces, and pig-faces.

sanskrit: yathā madvaśagā sītā kṣipraṃ bhavati jānakī tathā kuruta rākṣasyaḥ sarvāḥ kṣipraṃ sametya ca
english: "Do whatever must be done, all of you rākṣasīs, gathering quickly, so that Jānakī Sītā swiftly comes under my control."

sanskrit: pratilomānulomaiś ca sāmadānādibhedanaiḥ āvartayata vaidehīṃ daṇḍasyodyamanena ca
english: "Turn Vaidehī around by contrary and favorable means, by conciliation, by gifts, and by the threat of punishment."

sanskrit: iti pratisamādiśya rākṣasendraḥ punaḥ punaḥ kāmamanyuparītātmā jānakīṃ paryatarjayat
english: Having thus commanded them again and again, the lord of rākṣasas, his soul consumed by passion and fury, threatened Jānakī repeatedly.

sanskrit: upagamya tataḥ kṣipraṃ rākṣasī dhānyamālinī pariṣvajya daśagrīvam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then the rākṣasī Dhānyamālinī quickly approached and, embracing the ten-necked one, spoke these words.

sanskrit: mayā krīḍa mahārājasītayā kiṃ tavānayā akāmāṃ kāmayānasya śarīram upatapyate icchantīṃ kāmayānasya prītir bhavati śobhanā
english: "Sport with me, O great king — what use is this Sītā to you? When one who desires courts an unwilling woman, his body is tormented; when one who desires courts a willing woman, joy is fair and full."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rākṣasyā samutkṣiptas tato balī jvaladbhāskaravarṇābhaṃ praviveśa niveśanam
english: Thus addressed by the rākṣasī, that mighty one was lifted up and entered the inner dwelling that blazed with the radiance of the sun.

sanskrit: devagandharvakanyāś ca nāgakanyāś ca tās tataḥ parivārya daśagrīvaṃ viviśus tad gṛhottamam
english: Then those daughters of gods, gandharvas, and nāgas surrounded the ten-necked one and entered that excellent mansion.

sanskrit: sa maithilīṃ dharmaparām avasthitāṃ pravepamānāṃ paribhartsya rāvaṇaḥ vihāya sītāṃ madanena mohitaḥ svam eva veśma praviveśa bhāsvaram
english: Having threatened Maithilī — who stood firm in her devotion to righteousness, trembling — Rāvaṇa, deluded by passion, abandoned Sītā and entered his own luminous dwelling.

sanskrit: ity uktvā maithilīṃ rājā rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ saṃdiśya ca tataḥ sarvā rākṣasīr nirjagāma ha
english: Having spoken thus to Maithilī and having commanded all the rākṣasīs, King Rāvaṇa — the destroyer of enemies — departed.

sanskrit: niṣkrānte rākṣasendre tu punar antaḥpuraṃ gate rākṣasyo bhīmarūpās tāḥ sītāṃ samabhidudruvuḥ
english: When the lord of rākṣasas had gone out and returned to the inner apartments, those rākṣasīs of terrible form rushed at Sītā.

sanskrit: tataḥ sītām upāgamya rākṣasyaḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ paraṃ paruṣayā vācā vaidehīm idam abruvan
english: Then those rākṣasīs, maddened with rage, approached Sītā and spoke these words to Vaidehī in the harshest of tones.

sanskrit: paulastyasya variṣṭhasya rāvaṇasya mahātmanaḥ daśagrīvasya bhāryātvaṃ sīte na bahu manyase
english: "Sītā, you do not think highly of becoming the wife of the most excellent Paulastya — the great-souled Rāvaṇa, the ten-necked one."

sanskrit: tatas tv ekajaṭā nāma rākṣasī vākyam abravīt āmantrya krodhatāmrākṣī sītāṃ karatalodarīm
english: Then a rākṣasī named Ekajaṭā, red-eyed with anger, addressed Sītā — whose palms were as tender as her belly — and spoke these words.

sanskrit: prajāpatīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ tu caturtho yaḥ prajāpatiḥ mānaso brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ pulastya iti viśrutaḥ
english: "Among the six progenitors, the fourth lord of creatures is Pulastya — the mind-born son of Brahmā, renowned by that name."

sanskrit: pulastyasya tu tejasvī maharṣir mānasaḥ sutaḥ nāmnā sa viśravā nāma prajāpatisamaprabhaḥ
english: "And of Pulastya's mind-born son is the illustrious great sage Viśravā by name, equal in splendor to a lord of creatures."

sanskrit: tasya putro viśālākṣi rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ tasya tvaṃ rākṣasendrasya bhāryā bhavitum arhasi mayoktaṃ cārusarvāṅgi vākyaṃ kiṃ nānumanyase
english: "His son is Rāvaṇa, the destroyer of enemies, O wide-eyed one. You deserve to become the wife of that lord of rākṣasas. The words I have spoken, O beautiful-limbed one — why do you not consent to them?"

sanskrit: tato harijaṭā nāma rākṣasī vākyam abravīt vivṛtya nayane kopān mārjārasadṛśekṣaṇā
english: Then a rākṣasī named Harijaṭā, with eyes like a cat's, widening them in anger, spoke these words.

sanskrit: yena devās trayastriṃśad devarājaś ca nirjitaḥ tasya tvaṃ rākṣasendrasya bhāryā bhavitum arhasi
english: "By whom the thirty-three gods and even the king of gods were conquered — you deserve to become the wife of that lord of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: vīryotsiktasya śūrasya saṃgrāmeṣv anivartinaḥ balino vīryayuktasyā bhāryātvaṃ kiṃ na lapsyase
english: "Of one who is filled with valor, a hero who never retreats from battle, who is powerful and endowed with might — why would you not attain the status of wife?"

sanskrit: priyāṃ bahumatāṃ bhāryāṃ tyaktvā rājā mahābalaḥ sarvāsāṃ ca mahābhāgāṃ tvām upaiṣyati rāvaṇaḥ
english: "Setting aside his beloved and highly-regarded wives, that king of great might, Rāvaṇa — greatest among all — will come to you."

sanskrit: samṛddhaṃ strīsahasreṇa nānāratnopaśobhitam antaḥpuraṃ samutsṛjya tvām upaiṣyati rāvaṇaḥ
english: "Abandoning the inner apartments filled with a thousand women, adorned with jewels of every kind, Rāvaṇa will come to you."

sanskrit: asakṛd devatā yuddhe nāgagandharvadānavāḥ nirjitāḥ samare yena sa te pārśvam upāgataḥ
english: "He who has repeatedly defeated in battle gods, nāgas, gandharvas, and dānavas in combat — he has come to your side."

sanskrit: tasya sarvasamṛddhasyā rāvaṇasya mahātmanaḥ kimarthaṃ rākṣasendrasya bhāryātvaṃ necchase 'dhame
english: "Of that great-souled Rāvaṇa, fully prosperous in every way — why do you not desire, O base one, to be the wife of the lord of rākṣasas?"

sanskrit: yasya sūryo na tapati bhīto yasya ca mārutaḥ na vāti smāyatāpāṅge kiṃ tvaṃ tasya na tiṣṭhasi
english: "The sun does not burn out of fear of him; the wind does not blow in his presence — O woman of lovely glances, why do you not submit to him?"

sanskrit: puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ ca taravo mumucur yasya vai bhayāt śailāś ca subhru pānīyaṃ jaladāś ca yadecchati
english: "Trees out of fear of him let fall a rain of flowers; mountains yield water whenever he wishes; clouds yield rain at his will — O beautiful-browed one."

sanskrit: tasya nairṛtarājasya rājarājasya bhāmini kiṃ tvaṃ na kuruṣe buddhiṃ bhāryārthe rāvaṇasya hi
english: "Of that king of the nairṛtas, the king of kings, O passionate woman — why do you not turn your mind to becoming the wife of Rāvaṇa?"

sanskrit: sādhu te tattvato devi kathitaṃ sādhu bhāmini gṛhāṇa susmite vākyaṃ anyathā na bhaviṣyasi
english: "What has been truly told to you, O goddess, is truly well spoken, O passionate one. Accept these words, O sweet-smiling one — otherwise, things will not go well for you."
